about: Electronics' tools for agents (through Agent Link): name, what it does, its arguments as JSON Schema, its group, whether it changes the document.

card.does: Reads a KiCad board into the document (.kicad_pcb, KiCad 5 to 9).

path.means: The full path of the file

heights.means: The height of a component by ref: { "J1": mm }

minHeight.means: Components under it get no box

centre.means: true moves the middle of the board to the origin; false keeps KiCad's own coordinates, with y turned up

name.means: The name of the board (the file's name when left out)

links.line: A component's height comes from heights, else the footprint's STEP model, else a Height property on the footprint

effects: The file is parsed here
KiCad is not needed
It makes the board as a solid body "PCB <name>" from its Edge.Cuts outline and thickness
The cut-outs and mounting holes go through it
It makes each tall component as a box over its courtyard, a body each
The height of a component comes from the STEP model of the footprint, where this computer has it
Else the height comes from a Height property on the footprint
With no height known, no box is made, and noHeight lists the refs
moved says by how much the board moved
The bodies are plain Part solids
Every import adds a new board and components
The facts of the board (size, holes, footprints, edge connectors, the path of the file) are kept with the document
board_enclosure and pcb_order_package use the kept facts
A big board with hundreds of footprints takes several seconds
The answer of a changing call can also hold health from the shared check
A part with no STEP model and no Height property has no known height: heights { ref: mm } gives it.

board.means: The label of the board body made

copperLayers.means: How many copper layers the board has

holes.means: [{ at: [x, y], d, kind }] each hole in the board

footprints.means: How many footprints the board has

tall.means: [{ ref, value, side, height, from }] each tall component and where its height comes from

edgeConnectors.means: [{ ref, value, side, from, to, over }] footprints at the outline, with the side they meet

bodies.means: [labels] of the bodies made: the board, then its components

noHeight.means: the parts with no known height: { count, refs [first 20] }

openOutline.means: how many pieces of Edge.Cuts join nothing and were left out

moved.means: [x, y] the move that put the board middle at the origin

step.means: The undo step number of this call

refusalNotes: Refused: path is not a file
Refused: the file is not a board that KiCad 5 to 9 wrote
hints: Delete the old board and components (object_delete) before you import a changed file

kicad_import.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f8f209 (moved to Workshop Electronics)

card.does: Makes an enclosure round a board that kicad_import read, placed round it where it stands.

board.means: The label of the board (you can leave it out when one board is imported)

screw.means: The screw size, unless taken from the hole

standoff.means: The standoff height; overrides the clearance of the parts on the underside

headroom.means: The headroom; overrides the clearance of the tallest part on top

skip.means: Refs of edge connectors left closed

openings.means: More openings: [{ side: front|back|left|right, at, width, height, z }], as gen_part's board_box takes them
forms: { side: front|back|left|right, at, width, height, z }

links.line: standoff and headroom override the computed heights
skip leaves some connector openings closed; openings adds more

effects: It makes two new bodies: the box and its lid
The lid is laid beside, printed top down; turn it over about X to put it on
It puts a standoff under each mounting hole
The screw comes from the size of the hole, unless screw says so
The standoff height clears the parts on the underside
The headroom clears the tallest part on top
It opens the walls for the edge connectors that kicad_import found
Holes take the fit calibration of the printer (fit calibrate)
When no fit calibration is kept, holes are made 0.2 mm big, and printerFit says so
Each call adds a new box and lid
The answer of a changing call can also hold health from the shared check
The lid is laid beside the box, printed top down; turn it over about X to put it on.
A connector with no known height gets a 5 mm opening
Give its height in kicad_import, or openings by hand

board.means: The label of the imported board the box is for

bodies.means: [box, lid] the labels of the bodies made

outside.means: [x, y, z] outside size of the box

standoff.means: Height of the standoffs under the board

headroom.means: Room above the board's tallest part

standoffs.means: { screw, at, diameter, pilot, pilotDepth } the screw posts; absent without any

openings.means: Per opening: ..., for: the connector's ref or "given"

printerFit.means: calibrated: the calibration kept with the document; none: no calibration kept, holes assumed to print 0.2 mm small

sound.means: { label: true | false } whether each body is a sound solid

openingHeightGuessed.means: connectors with no known height: { refs, mm: the height used }

step.means: The undo step number of this call

openings.openAtRim.means: true on an opening that runs open at the rim

refusalNotes: Refused: several boards and none named
Refused: a name that is not an imported board
Refused: a value out of the range of board_box
hints: Use kicad_import first, or gen_part { generator: "board_box" } with the sizes by hand
Delete the old box and lid before you make it again
Give heights in kicad_import for connectors with no known height

board_enclosure.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f8f209 (moved to Workshop Electronics)

card.does: Packages the fabrication files of a board for ordering.

files.means: Full paths of the Gerbers, drill files, BOM and placement (CPL) files that KiCad's fabrication outputs wrote

board.means: The label of an imported board; the size of the board comes from it

size.means: The board size [x, y], else read from the outline Gerber

kicadPcb.means: A .kicad_pcb path for the design rule check; else the imported board's own file

links.line: Size comes from board, else size, else the outline Gerber

effects: Nothing is uploaded, ordered or paid for: the person does that
The files are sorted by kind
The order sheet says what to upload where for that house
It writes to the folder of the session: <name>_gerbers.zip (upload-ready), <name>_order.zip and <name>_ORDER.md
<name>_order.zip holds the Gerber zip, the assembly files and the order sheet
When kicad-cli is on the PATH of this computer, it runs KiCad's design rule check on kicadPcb
Otherwise drc says why the check was not run: an order is not checked until it is
Changes nothing in the document
Uploading and paying are the person's to do.

gerberZip.means: Path of the zip of Gerber and drill files

package.means: Path of the order zip: Gerber zip, ORDER.md, assembly and other files

vendor.means: The name of the board house the sheet is for

board.means: { size, layers, thickness } of the board

drc.means: the kicad-cli result { errors, warnings, unconnected, first }, or { run: false, reason: noKicadCli | noKicadPcb | failed, error }

warnings.noOutlineGerber.means: The board house cannot cut the board without an outline Gerber: Edge_Cuts, .gko, .gm1

warnings.noDrillFile.means: A board with holes needs a .drl file

warnings.assemblyNeedsBomAndCpl.means: Assembly needs both a BOM and a placement file, and one is given

refusalNotes: Refused: a path in files that is not a file
Refused: a board that was not imported
hints: When drc did not run, run Inspect › Design Rules Checker in KiCad before ordering
Fix its errors and unconnected items

card.does: Cuts a channel inside a body along a path, for a wire or a conductive trace.

body.means: The body to cut; a plain Part solid (Part::Feature)

path.means: [[x, y, z] ...], two or more points in document coordinates

section.means: { shape: round | square, size: 0.4 to 20 mm (the diameter or side; 2 when left out) }

bend.means: Corners are rounded to this: the size of the section or 2, whichever is more

material.means: For the trace resistance: carbon-pla | electrifi

awg.means: Wire gauge; gives the diameter of the wire, and its copper resistance

trace.means: false: no separate trace body with fill filament

links.line: fill filament also makes the trace as its own body "<body> trace" for a second material, unless trace: false
awg gives the wire diameter and copper resistance
Resistance of filament comes from material or from resistivity
Resistance comes from material or from resistivity
fill paint: the resistance comes the same way

effects: Each point is at least the size of the section from the one before
An end on a face of the part opens there; it is carried 1 mm past the face
An end inside stops blind
Between its ends, the channel must stay inside the part
A turn of over 170° is refused
fill wire: the channel takes the hole calibration of the printer
It also says whether the wire fits with 0.4 mm to spare
The channel is written into the body as a plain shape
Examples of a plain Part solid: an enclosure from board_enclosure or gen_part, an import, a part_transform copy
FreeCAD would rebuild a PartDesign Body or a parametric Part object and lose the channel
Face and edge numbers of the body change
A printed trace reads several times higher across layers than the figure given
The answer of a changing call can also hold health from the shared check
ohms is R = ρ·L/A on the channel's section, from typical resistivities; the filament's sheet is the authority.
Printed traces read higher across layers, several times up the Z axis.
The ohms of a wire are for solid copper at 20 °C
The insulation of a wire adds to the diameter, so check the wire's own

body.means: The label of the body the channel is cut in

bodies.means: [labels] the body, then the trace body when one is made

section.means: { shape, size, areaMm2 } the channel's cross-section

ends.means: [open | blind, ...] one per end of the path

bend.means: The radius the path corners are rounded to

sound.means: true: the body is a sound solid after the cut

conductor.means: { fill, resistivityOhmCm, ohms } for filament or paint; { fill, ohms: null, reason: noResistivity, material, materials } when the resistivity is not known; wire { awg, diameter, ohms, channelAtLeast, fits }

printerFit.means: calibrated or none: the printer fit calibration used

step.means: The undo step number of this call

refusalNotes: A PartDesign Body or a parametric Part object is refused, naming the plain copy to make
Refused too: the channel cuts nothing (the path is outside the part)
Refused too: it leaves the part unsound
hints: After a failed sweep, use fewer, longer segments or a larger bend
When the part is left unsound, move the path off the faces it grazes
Give resistivity, or a material from materials, when the resistivity is not known.
